quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A refund agent condenses the conversation every ten turns. At turn forty the condensed text says only that the customer awaits "a refund soon"; the sum and the promised day from turn six are gone, and the agent quotes something else. Which change fits best?

options.a: Keep amounts, dates and statuses in a structured block on each request
options.b: Condense each fifth turn instead, so that less is rounded off in each round
options.c: Ask the condensing prompt for longer summaries, with more detail kept in the prose
options.d: Send the full transcript on each request in place of the condensed text

explanation.a: The exact values leave the text that gets condensed, so no round of condensing can round them off.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Each round compresses the previous summary, so a detail that survived once can be rounded off the next time", and more rounds means more rounding.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A reader of the summary cannot tell that anything was lost", so more prose gives no check.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Resending the whole transcript is not the answer either".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A lookup returns 42 fields, and the agent needs five of them to decide on a return. After thirty lookups in one conversation, answers are slower and costlier. Which change fits best?

options.a: Move to a model with a bigger window so that all thirty results fit
options.b: Cut each result to its first 500 characters before it is kept in the chat
options.c: Pass on the handful the decision uses, word for word, plus an id
options.d: Rewrite each result as one sentence of prose before it is kept in the chat

explanation.c: The decision's fields are kept with their exact values and the rest is dropped before it accumulates.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the full result "is carried and paid for on every later request", whatever the window.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the advice is to "trim by a list written for the decisions the agent makes, not by length".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the fields are kept "with their exact values (never rounded or reworded)".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. At turn twelve a customer says the delivery address has changed. A delayed copy of the customer's turn-two message, which holds the old address, is processed afterwards. What should the facts store hold?

options.a: The old address, because it was the last one processed
options.b: The updated value as current, with the earlier one in the history
options.c: Both addresses as current values until the customer confirms one
options.d: The new address, with the old one deleted so that no trace remains

explanation.b: The date decides, so the late older value goes to the history and the current value is untouched.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Order of arrival does not decide".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a value with an earlier date is recorded in the history and does not replace anything", so nothing is left unsettled.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The old value is kept in the history, since an audit or a dispute may ask what was known when".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. One agent process serves many customers. After a deploy, customers see another customer's order details. The engineers find that the facts store was keyed by an id that the model copied from the conversation. What should they change?

options.a: Add a prompt rule telling the model to leave other people's data out of its replies
options.b: Empty the store hourly so that stale entries cannot be reached by anyone
options.c: Add the customer's name to each fact so that the model can tell them apart
options.d: Take the key from the authenticated session and filter where the context is built

explanation.d: The identity comes from the session the application holds, and the exclusion happens in code before the model sees anything.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A rule written in the prompt is not isolation".
explanation.c: Ruled out because facts of other customers are "excluded where the text is assembled, not left for the model to ignore".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the leak comes from the key, and the page's remedy is "Everything that is cached, remembered or summarised is scoped the same way", not a periodic clearing.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer returns after nine days. The facts block says the parcel is out for delivery, a state that the team treats as stale after a few hours. What should the agent do before replying?

options.a: Answer from the block, because stored facts outrank guesses
options.b: Ask the customer what the status was when they last looked
options.c: Read the value again from the order system and say which date applies
options.d: Discard every stored fact and rebuild the case from the customer's messages

explanation.c: A fact past its freshness limit is read again from the system of record, and the agent states the date it is going by.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a stale fact is a guess with a date on it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the remedy is to read the value again "from the system of record", not to ask the customer to recall it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the facts are valid until their limit, and the block is how the numbers survive: "the case facts block carries the numbers".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A synthesis agent receives forty findings from subagents as one long text, and its report leaves out findings from the middle of that text. Which change fits best?

options.a: Ask each subagent for longer explanations so that every finding takes more room
options.b: Open with a short digest of key points, then group detail under headers
options.c: Send the same forty findings twice so that each one appears in two places
options.d: Sort the findings alphabetically before they are joined into the input

explanation.b: Key findings go first under a header, with the detail under explicit headers.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the middle is where findings go missing", and longer text makes the middle longer.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide's remedy is placement: "Put the key findings and the case facts at the beginning of the aggregated input".
explanation.d: Ruled out because ordering by name changes nothing about where a finding sits: "Organise the detail under explicit headers".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer raises a late parcel and a billing error in one chat, each carrying a different sum, and later returns to the parcel. The agent mixes the sums. Which structure fits?

options.a: A single running total of the sums that spans both matters at once
options.b: One summary sentence that covers both matters and their sums
options.c: Dropping the first matter's data as soon as the second matter begins
options.d: A separate entry per matter with figures and dates, kept to closure

explanation.d: Each matter has its own entry, and no entry is dropped until the case closes.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "each issue has its own entry in the block, so that two refunds in one conversation never share an amount".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A reader of the summary cannot tell that anything was lost".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "no issue's entry is dropped until the case closes".
